1005649.headline: Alternates 2 search-call types, emitted through different routes and aimed in different directions.

facts.label: Bandwidth
facts.ambiguity: Some sources report a power-relative bandwidth (-3 dB or -10 dB) under the same word; those belong in bandwidth_3db / bandwidth_10db.

alternatives.note: Band stated to sit just below the type 2 band, with no or small overlap. Absolute start and end frequencies not given for type 1.

facts.label: End frequency
facts.ambiguity: Same threshold dependence as start_frequency. Many sources print 'minimum frequency' or 'Fmin' for this quantity, which is only equivalent when the sweep descends monotonically; those headings are registered to min_frequency, so a source using them for the sweep terminus must be mapped explicitly in its importer.

facts.label: Peak frequency
facts.ambiguity: Measured over the whole call in some studies and over the call body in others; FFT window and size change the value. Record the method's frequency_definition wherever stated.

alternatives.note: Used as the model input frequency for B. barbastellus.

facts.label: Start frequency
facts.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent: where the sweep is judged to begin varies with the dB threshold used, which is often unstated. Sources that print 'highest frequency' or 'Fmax' usually mean this for a downward FM sweep, but those headings are registered to max_frequency because they are literal; map them by hand per source rather than by alias.

facts.label: Pulse duration
facts.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent. Values measured from a spectrogram at an unstated dB threshold can differ by a factor of two from envelope-based measures.

alternatives.note: Measurement threshold not stated; not safely comparable with Seibert 2015.

facts.label: Source level
facts.ambiguity: Meaningless without a reference distance (10 cm and 1 m are both in use - a 20 dB difference) and without stating whether the value is rms or peak-equivalent. Both belong in the method record; a source level lacking a stated reference distance must be flagged.
facts.note: dB peSPL at 10 cm from the bat's mouth. Only type 1 calls were analysed, because 92% of moth detection distances were in response to this type. Compare Nyctalus leisleri at 127 dB peSPL under the same method.

facts.label: Source level
facts.ambiguity: Meaningless without a reference distance (10 cm and 1 m are both in use - a 20 dB difference) and without stating whether the value is rms or peak-equivalent. Both belong in the method record; a source level lacking a stated reference distance must be flagged.
facts.note: Absolute source level, dB SPL rms re 20 uPa at 1 m. Apparent source level reported separately as 79.9 ± 5.1.

facts.label: Moth detection distance
facts.ambiguity: Depends on the moth species, which auditory cell (A1 or A2) is used as the criterion, and the assumed hearing threshold. Record the criterion in notes; values using different criteria are not comparable.
facts.note: Field-measured distance at which the A1 auditory cell of the moth Noctua pronuba responds to the approaching bat. Nyctalus leisleri under the same criterion: 33.2 m. value_min/value_max are quartiles, not a range. Modelled prediction was 4.3 m [3.4-6.1 m].
